recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not remove PractitionerRole under FHIR-16100 unless a separate work-group decision explicitly reverses the later PractitionerRole alignment; this issue is resolved by the absence of Patient and RelatedPerson collector targets.
issue_request: FHIR-16100 was Published with Persuasive with Modification. Although the original Jira resolution text proposed removing PractitionerRole and allowing Patient/RelatedPerson, the Jira comments and later OO minutes record the accepted reversal: the BDP collector is the person performing the collection, not the donor/source, and Patient/RelatedPerson should be removed.
initial_application: Spreadsheet-era history shows an initial application followed by the reversal. Commit f8ce0d5631 applied the first proposal, and commit b4bd0b114e pre-applied the reversed direction by changing the collector reference from Practitioner|Patient|RelatedPerson to Practitioner and removing patient/related-person wording from the definition.
additional_context: BiologicallyDerivedProduct is active in source/fhir.ini. Commit 7475edc72c later added PractitionerRole back to BDP.collection.collector as part of a broader OO pass for missing PractitionerRole references; that later target is distinct from the Patient/RelatedPerson issue. OO HCP minutes from 2021-10-04 reopened FHIR-16100 and voted to remove Patient and RelatedPerson from the definition as applied to the current build.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/biologicallyderivedproduct/structuredefinition-BiologicallyDerivedProduct.xml defines collection.collector as a healthcare professional and targets only Practitioner and PractitionerRole, with no Patient or RelatedPerson target profile.
